cohort: 633 twin pregnancies and 1267 singleton pregnancies with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP)
finding: Twin pregnancies with ICP have a higher risk for adverse perinatal outcomes compared to singletons, and this risk is associated with elevated total bile acid (TBA) levels.
mod_finding: Twin pregnancies with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy had a higher risk of cesarean section compared to singletons (96.4% vs. 76.1%).
